question.text: Three blocks of masses 6 kg, 4 kg and 10 kg touch each other in a line on a frictionless horizontal floor, arranged in that order from left to right. A horizontal force of 100 N pushes on the outer face of the 6 kg block, directed rightward toward the other blocks, and a horizontal force of 40 N pushes on the outer face of the 10 kg block, directed leftward toward the other blocks. All surfaces, including the floor, are smooth.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the acceleration of each of the three blocks.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the net force acting on the 6 kg block, on the 4 kg block, and on the 10 kg block.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: Find the contact force between the 4 kg block and the 10 kg block.

conditions: blocks arranged touching each other, 6 kg then 4 kg then 10 kg left to right
100 N applied on 6 kg block, directed rightward
40 N applied on 10 kg block, directed leftward

figure.description: Three blocks rest touching each other on a horizontal frictionless floor, arranged left to right as 6 kg, 4 kg, 10 kg, with no gaps between them. A 100 N horizontal force pushes on the left (outer) face of the 6 kg block, directed rightward into the row of blocks. A 40 N horizontal force pushes on the right (outer) face of the 10 kg block, directed leftward into the row of blocks. Every contact surface, block-to-block and block-to-floor, is frictionless.

solution.approach: Treat the three blocks as one system to find the common acceleration, then isolate the 10 kg block to find the contact force with the 4 kg block.

steps.text: Find the net force and total mass of the three-block system.
The common acceleration of all three blocks follows from the net force and total mass.
The net force on each block equals its own mass times this common acceleration.
steps.equation: 6 kg block: 18 N, 4 kg block: 12 N, 10 kg block: 30 N

steps.text: Isolate the 10 kg block: the contact push from the 4 kg block, N, minus the 40 N force gives its net force.

final_answer.value: (a) a = 3 m/s²; (b) net force: 18 N on the 6 kg block, 12 N on the 4 kg block, 30 N on the 10 kg block; (c) force between the 4 kg and 10 kg blocks = 70 N

common_mistakes.text: Adding 100 N and 40 N instead of subtracting them, since both arrows point toward the middle of the row, giving a = 140/20 = 7 m/s².
Taking the contact force between the 4 kg and 10 kg blocks as the 40 N applied force, ignoring the 10 kg block's own net force, giving N = 40 N.
